author: Ronald Clark
title: USI men hope recent play is sustainable - NewsBreak
text:
By Ronald Clark ,
1 hours ago
HENDERSON, Ky (WEHT) – After beating Western Illinois by 32 points in the second night of a back-to-back, University of Southern Illinois men’s basketball head coach Stan Gouard said he hopes his team’s play is sustainable going forward.
The night before, the Screaming Eagles dropped an opportunity to get an overtime win over Eastern Illinois. Gouard said he and his team had a “come to Jesus moment” in the locker room following the loss. He said they spent about 30-45 minutes discussing their frustration and how they can improve their play.
In the matchup against the Leathernecks they finally lived up to their potential and played the exact way their coach has wanted them to execute. USI’s up-tempo offense scored nearly 100 points in their second Ohio Valley Conference win of the season. Now Gouard says they need to keep playing at their pace more consistently to stack some wins.
“I don’t care who we’re playing against, if it’s Western Illinois or Tennessee Tech it doesn’t matter,” he said. “You know winning at this level is hard and to secure a win the way we did it and with the differential in the points you know it was a tremendous confidence boost for our team. And hopefully you know going forward you know I think the confidence is there, we just got to see a few go in.”
Next, Southern Indiana will take on Lindenwood Thursday, January 29th, at 7:30 p.m. in the Liberty Arena. The game is scheduled to stream on ESPN Plus.
